measurement.trade_off: Do not copy illustrative values from the design reference. Show unavailable and empty states instead of invented scientific data. Keep the original startup flow and scientific gates unchanged.

evidence: The dashboard consumes existing /health, /v1/workspaces, /v1/workspaces/active, /v1/model, /v1/scientific-validation, /v1/jobs and /v1/catalog/results endpoints.
The light-curve panel plots only observations from a persisted result. No example light curve or sample object queue is inserted.
The dashboard shows exact fail-closed scientific validation status and blocker count. API health and model registry status are displayed separately.
The desktop navigation exposes only existing desktop views; experimental classification, feature and OOD views remain hidden.
The desktop CSS includes the reference's navy/blue visual system, responsive metric cards, panels and a local galaxy banner asset.
The Workbench header uses a scalable SVG brand asset. The previous ICO remains an alternate favicon and native Windows icon asset.
DR24 workspace preflight was separated from the source-acquisition error handler. No active workspace is shown as NOT RUN, and no DR24 request is sent.
The help page explains that a workspace must be created or opened before DR24 retrieval.

The Windows runtime workflow ran 31 tests in its last completed attempt; 31 passed and 1 failed because a test still expected the ICO to be the primary favicon. The test expectation was updated to require SVG primary and ICO fallback.

The browser workflow captured a 1600x1000 screenshot. Its preceding run failed because the test asserted the workspace-preflight text before awaiting the asynchronous request. The test now waits for the expected preflight response.

The browser screenshot from the earlier run showed the first dashboard layout and truthful empty states. It also exposed duplicate navigation because .nav-item display:flex overrode the hidden attribute. A targeted CSS rule now preserves hidden state, and the browser contract checks the visible navigation count and order.

The exact-head Product Scope Audit and CodeQL passed on a previous code head; the latest commits add the galaxy banner, navigation order, browser wait, package test and this cycle record, so all gates must run again on the final head.

root_causes: The prior desktop landing page was a raw Workbench/DR24 form and did not implement the supplied Scientific Mission Control design.
Desktop CSS display:flex overrode the browser's hidden state on legacy navigation items, making old and new navigation entries appear together.

The DR24 workspace prerequisite was checked inside the DR24 acquisition catch block. A missing workspace was therefore displayed as a source-acquisition failure even though no source request had been sent.
The first browser contract assertion did not wait for the asynchronous workspace preflight result.
A Windows runtime test still asserted that the ICO was the primary favicon after the header/favicon changed to SVG.

findings: A design mockup is not a data fixture. All scientific values and operational statuses must come from real API responses or persisted records.
API process liveness, data-source availability, model registry state and scientific validation are distinct states and must not be conflated.
When no saved observation data exists, an empty light-curve state is more correct than a synthetic chart.
The active-workspace prerequisite must be checked before DR24 acquisition. A preflight failure is NOT RUN, not an acquisition failure.
CSS display rules must preserve the semantic HTML hidden attribute for navigation items.
Browser tests must wait for asynchronous UI state before asserting it.
Source static assets added to the desktop UI must be included in the frozen self-test and packaged asset set.
A browser screenshot supports visual review but does not replace a real installed Windows WebView2 screenshot.

Verify the latest packaged app preserves Splash Screen, automatic handoff and visible Workbench.
Verify Desktop and Start Menu shortcut icon and taskbar icon on installed Windows. Issue #320 remains open for the native Windows icon investigation.
Compare the installed Windows application screenshot with the founder-supplied reference before accepting the UX redesign.
Do not describe AI classification, rare-object discovery, or scientific validation as accepted capabilities unless their own gates pass.
